newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Gramm seeks muni bond provisions in tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Gramm seeks muni bond provisions in tax plan.

text.p: Sen. Bob Graham on Wednesday urged Senate Finance Committee members to include five provisions backed by the municipal bond industry in a tax package the panel is expected to begin considering next week.

Graham, a Florida Democrat who is a member of the finance panel, said in an eight-page memo to committee members that the proposals would help communities construct and repair schools by "reducing the cost of financing and by providing access to tax-exempt financing for private entities."
One proposal would increase from $10 million to $25 million the amount of bonds that localities could issue annually that could be purchased by banks, according to Graham's memo.
Another provision would raise the small issuer rebate exception from $5 million to $25 million and provide a rebate safe-harbor for long term fixed-rate debt, Graham's memo said.
Graham's plan also would create a category of exempt facility bonds for qualified education facilities and make the category exempt from the current volume cap, the memo said.
Graham would modify depreciation rules to allow facilities that are financed with tax-exempt bonds to receive accelerated depreciation.
Finally, Graham called for an increase in the $150 million cap on the amount of tax-exempt bonds that can be issued by non-profit 501(c)(3) institutions, including universities and colleges.
